title: Cross-SDK idempotency and backoff ergonomics: practical defaults, error taxonomy, and language examples
creator: Lena Chen
description: Ship opinionated, cross-language defaults and ergonomic APIs for retry/backoff policies and idempotency keys across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Provide a clear retryable-error taxonomy, streaming-specific semantics, and worked examples that reduce developer confusion and production incidents.
background: Multiple teams are implementing retry logic inconsistently across SDKs. Current gaps: different default backoff parameters, ad-hoc idempotency key generation, no explicit guidance for streaming endpoints, and mismatched retryable error lists. This causes customer misconfigurations, duplicated effort, and reliability incidents when SDK defaults are too aggressive or too conservative.
goals: 1) Define a single source-of-truth retryable error taxonomy and default backoff parameters. 2) Provide a clear idempotency key convention and helper utilities in each SDK. 3) Document streaming retry semantics and provide example patterns. 4) Ship SDK changes with migration notes and telemetry to evaluate impact.
non_goals: 1) Server-side idempotency enforcement beyond existing API behavior. 2) Substantive protocol changes (we will not add new HTTP endpoints). 3) Rewriting transport layers in each SDK unrelated to retry/idempotency behavior.
proposal: - Standardize defaults: initial_backoff_ms=100, max_backoff_ms=2000, multiplier=2.0, jitter=full_jitter. - Retry window: retry up to 4 attempts by default (initial + 3 retries). - Idempotency key: header 'X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key' with 128-bit UUID v4 by default and optional deterministic generator for user-supplied request fingerprinting. - TTL for server-side idempotency expected: 24 hours (documented). - Retryable errors: canonical list below (includes 429, 502, 503, 504, connection/reset/timeout). - Streaming semantics: for single-request streaming (server sends chunks), do not automatically retry mid-stream; provide transparent reconnect + resume using per-request sequence tokens where model/protocol supports it. - Expose high-level RetryPolicy object in each SDK with safe defaults but straightforward overrides.
retryable_error_taxonomy: Recommended canonical retryable categories: 1) Transient server overload: 429 (rate limit) when Retry-After not present -> retry with backoff; if Retry-After present prefer honoring it. 2) Infrastructure errors: 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable, 504 Gateway Timeout -> retry. 3) Network errors: connection reset, TLS handshake failure, DNS resolution errors, socket timeouts -> retry. 4) Client-side idempotency failures: 409 conflict when server indicates request already applied -> do not retry; surface to caller. 5) Application errors (4xx other than 429/409) -> do not retry. Edge cases: 500 Internal Server Error -> retry by default but include a sampling rate to avoid replay amplification for non-idempotent operations.
backoff_defaults_and_rationale: We selected a short initial backoff (100ms) for low-latency workloads and small multiplier (2x) to keep total retry window bounded. Full jitter prevents thundering herds. Max backoff 2s keeps latency budgets reasonable for interactive apps. Default 4 attempts balances successful recoveries vs cost/duplicate risk.
idempotency_conventions: - Header: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key (string). - Generation: SDK default uses RFC4122 UUID v4 keyed to user context. - Deterministic option: SDK method generate_deterministic_idempotency_key(payload_fields: list[str], secret_salt: str) that returns a stable HMAC-SHA256 truncated base64 string. - Length: recommend <=128 chars. - Scope: keys are tenant-scoped; avoid global collisions by prefixing with tenant id when available. - TTL expectations: document 24h server retention; warn users when relying on >24h semantics. - Behavior when header omitted: SDK will attach a UUID v4 unless the call is marked explicitly non-idempotent.
sdk_api_changes: Python: add redwood.RetryPolicy and redwood.utils.idempotency.generate_deterministic_key(), default client behavior attaches idempotency header. TypeScript: export RetryPolicy, ClientOptions.retryPolicy, idempotency util in @redwood/sdk. Go: add type RetryPolicy and helper IdempotencyKeyGenerator function. All languages: expose constants for defaults and a means to opt into: ClientOptions.retryPolicy = RetryPolicy.Default.WithMaxAttempts(6).
sdk_language_examples:
Python example:
from redwood import Client, RetryPolicy, utils
client = Client(api_key=..., retry_policy=RetryPolicy.default())
payload = {'prompt': 'hello'}
# client will attach X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key automatically
resp = client.generate_text(payload)

Go example:
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithAPIKey(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY")), redwood.WithRetryPolicy(redwood.DefaultRetryPolicy()))
key := redwood.GenerateDeterministicIdempotencyKey([]string{"user:123", "hash:abcd"}, "org-salt")
resp, err := client.GenerateText(ctx, req, redwood.WithIdempotencyKey(key))
streaming_semantics: - Stream types: unary-response-stream (one request, many tokens) vs bidirectional. - For unary-response-stream: do not automatically retry once server started producing tokens; expose client.ResumeStream(token_offset) when the server supports resume tokens. - For bidirectional: provide connectors that buffer a small amount of user input and only retry the last unacknowledged unit. - Provide explicit examples and an opt-in auto-retry mode for streams with idempotent server-side resume support.
migration_notes: - Defaults will change in patch: SDKs will start attaching idempotency header by default. We will document this and provide opt-out via ClientOptions.disableIdempotencyHeader=true. - Provide a compatibility flag for teams who relied on previous retry counts. - Communicate changes in SDK release notes with guidance for heavy-throughput integrations.
implementation_tasks: Add RetryPolicy types and default constants to Python/TS/Go SDKs
Implement idempotency helper utilities (UUID v4 + deterministic HMAC) in each SDK
Add header injection in transport layer with opt-out flag
Add streaming resume helpers and small client tests for resume behavior
Update SDK docs, quickstarts, and changelogs
Add unit + integration tests and chaos tests for transient errors
Create telemetry events: retry_attempt, idempotency_header_sent, resume_attempt
test_plan: - Unit tests for deterministic idempotency key generation across languages. - Integration tests that simulate 502/503/connection resets and assert SDK retries follow backoff defaults. - Streaming tests: assert no automatic mid-stream retry; resume helpers return correct offsets. - Canary rollout: enable new SDK default behavior for 10% of early-access customers and monitor error/latency rates.
monitoring_and_metrics: Emit telemetry events for: retry_attempt (tags: error_code, attempt_index), retry_policy_override, idempotency_header_sent (tags: sdk_language), stream_resume_attempt (tags: success/failure). Create dashboard charts for retry rate, success-after-retry ratio, and incidents linked to idempotency collisions.
rollout_plan: 1) Land SDK changes behind feature flags. 2) Publish SDK beta releases with clear migration docs. 3) Monitor canary cohort (10%) for 2 weeks. 4) Promote to GA and update 'default' flag. 5) Follow up with users who opt-out for compatibility issues.
